title: TON oscillator and output feedback
summary: Complete a {{t:500}} ms Ladder blinker made of two TON timers and SET and RESET coils, and check its on and off times with FOR and AT assertions.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how bright a real lamp is or how exactly a real controller keeps the period.
objectives: Read a two-timer Ladder oscillator: each timer runs in one half period and starts the next.
Make the output change state by itself, from the time that each timer measures.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Blinky.ld.json the two timer rungs are already drawn: OffTimer runs while LED_Output is OFF and OnTimer runs while it is ON. Nothing changes LED_Output yet. Make the LED blink: OFF for about {{t:500}} ms, then ON for about {{t:500}} ms, again and again.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which timer runs while the LED is OFF, which one runs while it is ON, and why the LED must remember its state between scans.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict LED_Output at {{t:250}}, {{t:750}}, {{t:1250}}, and {{t:1750}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: OFF at {{t:250}} ms, ON at {{t:750}}, OFF at {{t:1250}}, ON at {{t:1750}}; the first rising edge lands between {{t:400}} and {{t:600}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program has the two timers but nothing that changes LED_Output, so the LED stays OFF for ever. Change it so that LED_Output blinks on its own: OFF for about {{t:500}} ms, then ON for about {{t:500}} ms, again and again. Leave the two timer rungs as they are.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named BlinkyVisual and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Review the trace and table: OFF until about {{t:500}} ms, ON until about {{t:1000}} ms, OFF again, then ON from about {{t:1500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: The three FOR windows ({{t:20}}-{{t:400}} ms OFF, {{t:620}}-{{t:900}} ms ON, {{t:1120}}-{{t:1400}} ms OFF) hold, and both rising edges and the falling edge are found.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What would the LED do with a single timer fed by the LED itself? And with a rung that turns the LED ON but no rung that turns it OFF?
stages.checkpoint: With one timer, the LED turning ON resets that timer at once, so the LED is ON for a single scan instead of blinking. Without the rung that turns it OFF, the LED turns ON once and stays ON for ever.

hints.text: Look at the first two rungs: OffTimer only runs while LED_Output is OFF and OnTimer only while it is ON, so something has to flip LED_Output when each one finishes.
Add a rung with a normally open contact on OffTimer.Q and a SET coil on LED_Output, and another with a contact on OnTimer.Q and a RESET coil on LED_Output.

faultCases: The starting program has the two timers but nothing that changes LED_Output, so the LED stays OFF for ever.
